title: R’ Yirmeyah Kahana
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman cites Bereshit Rabbah 7:4: he asked Resh Lakish, “One who mates [an animal] with a sea creature—what is the law?” Kahana objects; “here Kahana tore his net over R’ Shimon ben Lakish.” Hyman says this was copied incorrectly: the source is Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:6, where Kahana asks R’ Shimon ben Lakish about one who mates, etc. Bava Kamma 55a has R’ Yirmeyah reporting in Resh Lakish’s name: “One who mates,” etc. Hyman says that from this arose the Bereshit Rabbah wording “R’ Yirmeyah Kahana asked Resh Lakish”; he says it SHOULD READ: “R’ Yirmeyah said: Kahana asked R’ Shimon ben Lakish.”

notes.text: The supplied פרם means “tore,” whereas the checked Kilayim text has פרס, “spread,” and says Kahana caught Resh Lakish in the net. This verb difference remains a source question. Hyman’s re-punctuation separates Yirmeyah the reporter from Kahana the questioner.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Kilayim1:6 comparison has פרס, spread, beside supplied פרם, tore; recurring letter patterns do not establish print history. Hyman’s copying-history explanation is attributed, and his SHOULD READ force separates Yirmeyah the reporter from Kahana the questioner without an admitted identity correction. The question concerns mating [an animal] WITH A SEA CREATURE, not simply breeding sea creatures. All three locations and the source’s etc. remain. Resh Lakish is a conventional name reading of ר״ל; uninspected רשב״ל expands to R’ Shimon ben Lakish without an unsupported full Rabbi title.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 815) reads פרם, “tore.” The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 7:4 and Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:6 both read פרס, “spread.” The midrash first has Resh Lakish cast his net for Kahana, and then Kahana casts his for Resh Lakish. It joins Yirmeyah and Kahana in the question, while Kilayim explicitly has Yirmeyah report Kahana’s question. Bava Kamma 55a has Yirmeyah transmit a ruling in Resh Lakish’s name about crossing two species from the sea. Hyman’s proposed history of how the midrash’s wording arose remains his explanation.
